### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **13** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-memory`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/knowledge-memory`, `@objectstack/knowledge-ragflow`, `@objectstack/plugin-dev`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **106** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **13** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/package.json`, `packages/core/src/egress.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-memory/vitest.config.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **13** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/package.json`, `packages/core/src/egress.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-memory/vitest.config.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`
- **41** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **189** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `136f94be7881fcd7a0b0946b17703d6a56ebfcb3` — the merge of head `e022b2d6a9b4d58459b0b78bc7a08d0cb51b9824` into base `8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 136f94be7881fcd7a0b0946b17703d6a56ebfcb3 && git checkout 136f94be7881fcd7a0b0946b17703d6a56ebfcb3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9 e022b2d6a9b4d58459b0b78bc7a08d0cb51b9824 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9 && git merge --no-ff e022b2d6a9b4d58459b0b78bc7a08d0cb51b9824

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8436f67a2d522e0c700c37b69b22a083a30ce4b9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Read at 2026-11-16T06:11Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6908738958; no lane request (owed per check-owed-reviews). Independence: implemented in a project thread for security#1; reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

No prior contract-review record exists for this PR, so no earlier finding id is continued; M1, S1 to S3 and N1 to N3 are all new on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Declaration.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial on both the PR body and the changeset and agree with the diff: nothing an author can write is added, removed or re-valued; what moves is which destinations two outbound doors may reach, decided by operator environment at boot. The ADR-0087 `not-required` disposition holds for the same reason.
- **Doors named in the declaration.** Webhook deliveries and durable flow callouts have one send site in `service-messaging` and its default is the guard; the flow `http` node's inline arm, which is also the durable arm's no-outbox fallback, has one send site in `service-automation` and it is the guard. No second send site exists in either package or in `plugin-webhooks` on this head. No shipped plugin reaches either send site without the guard. Held.
- **Decision at the moment of connection.** The verdict is taken on the addresses the connection is made to, the connection goes to a judged address without a second resolution, each redirect hop is judged, a policy that throws refuses, and no caller can substitute its own transport. Held.
- **Boot.** A malformed or over-broad allowlist fails init in all three plugins; there is no unguarded fallback and no `NODE_ENV` branch. Held.
- **Controls.** Each refusal family has a paired control that delivers (allowlisted address, allowlisted host, allowed redirect, non-refusal transport failure still retried), the implementer's ablation of the refusal turned the three sending suites red, and the fixtures open loopback through the environment only. The readings in the PR body were taken at `28edf362a`; the two later commits and the merge are covered by this head's CI, not by those readings.
- **The rule's never tier and its "public" word.** Not held as declared: M1 and S1 below.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on all five packages with the BREAKING banner, the Who-moves paragraph and the one-line fix: correct for a non-protocol narrowing under AGENTS.md (the level follows the metadata kind, which is `none`). The new `@objectstack/core/egress` subpath, the three `egressPolicy` options and the two ledger codes are additive and ride the same level; `undici` is a runtime dependency of `@objectstack/core` and the lockfile agrees.

CI on this head: 69 check-runs, all completed, 60 success, 9 skipped, none failing or pending. The PR is open and mergeable-clean against `main`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **First-wave scope (dev flag).** Accepted as ruled for the two named doors. Escalated to the seat: the review inputs carry no tracking reference for the follow-up wave, so the seat confirms it is tracked in the private lane before landing; see S3 for the wording that must not outrun the scope meanwhile.
- **Proxy (dev flag).** These requests no longer use an environment-configured HTTP proxy. It is stated in the changeset's For-hosts paragraph; answered, with the note that it is an operator-facing change sitting under a hosts heading.
- **Not measured: a real public target (dev flag).** Not accepted as closed: see S2, which is exactly the part a stand-in on one loopback address cannot show.
- **Dogfood battery (dev flag).** Owed on the final head; the seat carries the reading before landing.
- **Author.** The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.
- **SQL push-down.** No new id materialisation and no in-app join. The boot census reads `sys_webhook` once and judges each row in the application because the judgement needs name resolution, which no query can push down; see N3 for its unbounded read.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes real a refusal the platform owed and takes away, at the consumer, only what the declaration names: internal targets need an operator allowlist entry. The seam (one decision per connected address, with host, organization and source, fail-closed) is the right shape and mirrors the datasource connect policy. Against the rule as written, the head does not yet hold in four places. Mechanism-level detail for M1 and S1 is in the sealed notes only.

- M1 (must-fix) — The rule says cloud metadata addresses are never reachable and can never be allowlisted. The default policy's never tier does not hold that for the whole class the rule names. Complete the tier and pin each added member both ways (refused by default, refused under a covering allowlist entry) with a neighbouring control. Specifics: sealed notes, M1.
- S1 (should-fix) — The rule's sentence is "only public addresses"; the default policy decides by an enumerated set of classes, and the two do not coincide. Either make the classification answer the sentence, or restate the sentence everywhere as the enumerated classes the Clause-② line already lists. Specifics: sealed notes, S1.
- S2 (should-fix) — The changeset promises that requests to public targets are unaffected, and the PR body records that delivery to a real public target was not measured. The guard dials one of the addresses it judged and does not fall back to the others, which the bare fetch it replaces did. A public target that answers on more than one address or family can therefore fail where it delivered before. Dial the judged addresses in turn, or state the changed behaviour in Who-moves; add a control with a first address that does not accept and a second that does.
- S3 (should-fix) — The changeset body and the policy's own header state the rule for every outbound request a tenant can aim, while the scope ruled for this PR is two doors. The release note must claim what ships: scope those sentences to webhook deliveries and the flow `http` node, as the title, the Clause-② line and the boot line already do. Prose-face and jsdoc only.
- N1 (nit) — The connect-time re-judgement of the socket's own remote address has no pin; the dial-the-judged-address property is pinned only indirectly, through the controls.
- N2 (nit) — In `webhook-outbox-plugin.ts` the new `bootEgressCensus` sits between `bootWebhookTable` and its jsdoc, so that comment now documents the wrong method.
- N3 (nit) — The census reads every `sys_webhook` row, whole, with no projection or bound; and the default guard keeps the logger of whichever plugin installed it first.

M1 and S1 to S3 are open. A delta read by this reviewer is owed on the next head.
